## Iguazu Bird Park: walking among macaws, toucans and tropical greenery

**Parque das Aves** is in Foz do Iguaçu, near the entrance to the Brazilian side of Iguazu National Park. Visitors follow a path among tropical vegetation and learn about South American birds. Some of the most memorable moments take place inside large aviaries reached by specially designed walkways: macaws, parrots and other birds may fly nearby.

The site's main value lies in the chance to see birds at close range and learn how the wildlife of the **Atlantic Forest (Mata Atlântica)** is protected. The park engages in conservation, education and research. This defines the experience: the walk takes place in a managed natural setting and purpose-built aviaries rather than on a wild forest trail where a rare bird sighting is entirely a matter of chance.

## What you may see on a visit

Among the most recognizable residents are **brightly colored macaws**, large-billed toucans, parrots, flamingos and other birds. The exhibits may change, and at certain times some birds are housed in areas closed to visitors for care or health reasons. It is therefore better to regard the visit as an introduction to a whole conservation program than as a promise of photographing one particular animal.

In the **immersive aviaries**, visitors enter an enclosed area on designated paths while the birds can move freely within their own space. This creates an unusual feeling of closeness to nature. But interaction is subject to clear rules: visitors must not feed, touch or chase birds to take photographs unless staff explicitly permit a particular activity.

The park also has areas with other animals and butterflies. Check official information shortly before visiting for the actual exhibits and access to particular spaces. Its overall purpose remains an introduction to biodiversity and conservation in the Iguazu region.

| Your interest | What the park offers |
| --- | --- |
| Toucans and macaws | Close-range observation |
| Tropical forest | A walk surrounded by greenery |
| Ecology | Learning about species conservation |
| Families with children | An educational route |
| Nature photography | Images without contact with birds |

## How the Bird Park differs from wild birdwatching

Watching wild birds in Brazil's forests and wetlands generally requires patience, time and a suitable season. At Parque das Aves, visitors follow a prepared route through aviaries, where the animals can be seen much closer. This makes the park a convenient introduction to characteristic species, including for those visiting South America for the first time.

But conservation parks and birdwatching in the wild serve different purposes. Here, visitors can recognize species, observe their behavior and learn about threats to their habitats. Encounters with free-ranging birds in natural conditions require separate nature excursions and compliance with protected-area rules. The [Nature and Wildlife](/interests/wildlife/) section helps compare these formats without confusing their characteristics.

An important part of Parque das Aves' context is the **Atlantic Forest**, a biome spanning parts of Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay that has been greatly reduced by human activity. Iguazu National Park protects a large area of this forest. Stories of bird rescue and conservation connect individual species with the question of where and under what conditions they can survive in the wild.

## Combining the park with Iguazu Falls

A major advantage of the location is its proximity to the Brazilian national park and [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). It is possible to visit both attractions on the same day, but decide beforehand how much time to allocate to each.

**The Brazilian side of the falls** is especially known for panoramic waterfall views and observation walkways. **Parque das Aves** offers a completely different focus: birds and forest ecology. Combining the two makes for a varied day; after the roar of the falls, a quieter walk among greenery offers a change of pace.

Admission to the national park and to Parque das Aves, however, involves **separate tickets**. Nearby entrances do not imply a combined ticket or included excursion. If an Ada Tours itinerary lists only the Brazilian falls, the Bird Park cannot be assumed to be included without an explicit mention. Check the selected journey's description for the exact excursions and tickets provided.

Unlike the Argentine side of Iguazu, the Bird Park is **in Brazil**. Travelers staying in Puerto Iguazú, Argentina, need to cross an international border to reach it. Visa requirements and entry rules depend on nationality and should be checked against current official sources when planning the route.

## How much time to allow

A visit to the Bird Park involves more than a single viewpoint. Foz do Iguaçu tourist information describes **a walking trail of approximately 1.5 km** through forest and aviaries. Allow several hours, with time to stop and watch the birds. An unhurried walk is more rewarding than rushing through every zone against the clock.

Part of the route has accessibility features, but wheelchair arrangements, assistance and conditions for visitors with limited mobility should be confirmed in advance. Comfortable closed-toe shoes, water and light clothing for sun or possible rain are useful in the humid tropical climate. Respect restrictions on flash photography and other rules posted by the park's staff.

If you also plan to visit the waterfalls, check opening times for both attractions and allow for transfers, queues and travel from your hotel. Do not assume hours are identical year-round. Plan meals and the return trip separately: an on-site café does not mean lunch is included in your excursion ticket.

## Why the park matters for Atlantic Forest conservation

Parque das Aves specializes in protecting Mata Atlântica birds and provides environmental education. The organization reports work in bird rescue and rehabilitation, scientific research and support for conservation initiatives. Visiting offers an insight into how animal care, visitor education and habitat protection relate to one another.

Toucans and macaws draw attention with their colorful plumage, but the deeper issue is forest fragmentation and the loss of suitable habitats. Observe the birds respectfully, avoid disturbing them and follow posted instructions. The experience becomes richer when you learn not only a species' name but also what is involved in its conservation.

For a Latin American journey, the park can be a first introduction to the region's rich birdlife. A separate nature excursion with an experienced guide could be a next step, but it should be chosen on the basis of its actual program.

## Frequently asked questions about the Bird Park

### Where is Parque das Aves?

In Foz do Iguaçu near the Brazilian entrance to Iguazu National Park. It is convenient to combine the visit with [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) if you allow time for both attractions.

### Can you see toucans and macaws up close?

The park has large aviaries and paths where guests can observe birds from a short distance. However, sightings of particular species and access to individual areas depend on animal care arrangements. Visitors may not feed or touch birds on their own.

### Is the Bird Park included in an Iguazu Falls ticket?

No. It is a separate attraction with its own tickets and visiting arrangements. It is included in a tour only where specifically listed among excursions or services.

### How is a park visit different from birdwatching?

The walk follows designated paths through aviaries and a managed conservation display. Birdwatching means observing free-ranging birds, whose appearance cannot be guaranteed. Both formats are worthwhile, but the experiences and purposes differ.

## Tours with an optional visit to Iguazu Bird Park

The [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) lies beside the Brazilian entrance to Iguazu National Park, near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Visitors can see toucans, macaws, parrots and other Atlantic Forest birds during a walk. The site is particularly convenient to add to a journey that already covers the Brazilian side of the waterfalls.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} where **the Bird Park can be visited in addition to the main itinerary**. A park visit is possible on these journeys, but it is not one of their guaranteed core stops. This distinction determines how much free time to leave and which services to arrange in advance.

## Why the Bird Park complements the waterfalls

The region's headline attraction is [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where travelers walk along designated paths and viewpoints to see the cascades. The Bird Park reveals a different aspect of local nature: birdlife among Atlantic Forest vegetation and the work of conserving rare species.

The Parque das Aves operator describes a path of approximately **2 km**, passing through several spacious immersive aviaries. Visitors follow designated walkways and can see birds from relatively close range. Touching the animals is prohibited. Educational staff help explain their habitats.

The official site confirms that the Bird Park and Brazilian waterfalls can be visited **on the same day**, as the attractions are close together. On a particular tour, though, this depends on the hours allocated, transport, flight times and the main program. A large group needs more time to assemble and move between locations than independent travelers.

## Which journeys offer the additional option?

On the [New Year “Brazil, Argentina and Chile” tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/), the Bird Park is listed **as a separately paid optional service**. The price in this specific itinerary is **$50 per person**. Macuco Safari is mentioned alongside it in the additional services, but this is a separate boat excursion and must not be confused with the Bird Park walk.

The [14-day “Best of Argentina” journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) also lists the site among potential destinations, but not among mandatory itinerary stops. The journey covers Bariloche, Patagonia, Ushuaia and the waterfalls, so any optional visit should be judged by how busy the particular Iguazu day is.

Other [tours through Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/tour/) differ in the number of nights and positioning of mandatory excursions. On a short trip, decide in advance which matters most: Brazilian viewpoints, the Argentine side, a boat ride or the Bird Park. No arbitrary combination can be promised in one day without checking the actual timetable.

## How the visit works

The park focuses on Atlantic Forest species and conservation. Staff explain population recovery and animal care. Highlights include a spacious macaw aviary and observations of toucans. This is a separate nature attraction, not part of the waterfall national park's trails.

Before choosing an excursion, check whether admission is included, how much walking time is allocated, whether transport is provided between the sites and where the group meets its guide. A park listed among **optional** places does not automatically grant admission or promise a dedicated guide.

The designated paths are generally suitable for a broad range of visitors, but hot, humid weather and rain affect comfort. Lightweight closed-toe shoes, water and weather-appropriate clothing make the walk more pleasant. Check opening hours directly with the operator for your visit date.

## Choosing a trip with children

For a family journey, the Bird Park can be an especially interesting addition after the noisy waterfalls: children can watch birds and learn how they are protected. Yet traveling with children does not mean admission, a special excursion or an interactive activity is already included.

For a wider selection, browse the [Brazil tours directory](/brazil/tour/) and [Nature tours in Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/). Compare actual Iguazu days rather than just tour names: an optional walk through bird aviaries does not mean wild-animal watching is included in the core program.

## Frequently asked questions about an optional excursion

### Can the Bird Park and waterfalls be visited in one day?

Yes. The park is beside the Brazilian entrance to the falls. Combining both walks depends on the tour schedule.

### Is the Bird Park included in every tour listed here?

No. These are programs where the visit **can be added**. Tickets, transport and payment depend on the specific journey.

### How long does the walk take?

The park's official route is about 2 km and passes through several themed aviaries. Duration depends on your pace and stops; the exact time on a tour must be arranged separately.

### How much does a visit cost?

The [three-country New Year tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) specifies $50 per person for the optional Bird Park. This is a condition of that particular program, not a universal admission price.

## Tours visiting Iguazu Bird Park: choosing a program

The [Iguazu Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) (Parque das Aves) lies in the Brazilian city of Foz do Iguaçu beside the entrance to the waterfall national park. Visitors can follow an Atlantic Forest trail, enter spacious aviaries and observe toucans, macaws and other birds close up. The park conserves rare species, and a visit takes the form of a walk through a conservation facility. This differs from a photographic safari to observe free-ranging animals.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including the Bird Park in the main itinerary. The key questions are **how much time is spent at Iguazu, which side of the falls is visited, what is included in the price and how busy each day will be**. For details of the attraction itself, see the [Bird Park page](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/); here we compare the journeys.

## Three ways to include the Bird Park in your trip

### A short three-day journey

[“3 Days in Foz do Iguaçu: Both Sides of the Falls and the Bird Park”](/brazil/tour/foz-do-iguacu-three-days/) is entirely devoted to the waterfalls and nearby natural attractions. On day one, travelers visit the Brazilian side of the cascades and the Bird Park. Day two features the Argentine side, including the [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/) area, while day three is reserved for departure.

The tour provides 2 nights at Vivaz Cataratas 4* or a similar hotel, breakfast, transfers, a Russian-speaking guide and admission to the principal attractions. **Macuco Safari is an additional service** here, so the boat excursion must not automatically be counted as part of the base price. This option suits visitors wishing to spend several days around Iguazu without continuing to other Brazilian regions.

### Corporate incentive with Macuco Safari

[“Iguazu in 3 Days: Both Sides of the Falls and Macuco Safari”](/brazil/tour/iguazu-incentive-3-days/) is designed for a corporate group. The Bird Park is scheduled on day two after the panoramic walkways on the Brazilian side and the Macuco Safari boat section. The same itinerary includes a Rafain dinner show and Argentine asado.

It is a busy format combining excursions with shared events. It is appropriate when the group wants collective experiences rather than only a quiet walk through nature. The hotel, group composition and price quotation for the incentive program are arranged separately; **the price of the standard three-day tour cannot be applied to it**.

### Bird Park on a 17-day itinerary

The [grand tour through Chile and Argentina, with Iguazu in Brazil](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) allocates **day 14** to the Brazilian side of the waterfalls, Macuco Safari and the Bird Park. Day 15 is devoted to the Argentine side. The remaining days are divided between Chile, Argentina and other stops on the route.

This option makes sense if you wish to see several countries and different natural regions of South America. The Bird Park is one stop on a much larger journey. If Iguazu Falls are your main goal, a compact itinerary concentrates more of the available time on this region.

| Program | Bird Park visit |
|---|---|
| [Iguazu, 3 days](/brazil/tour/foz-do-iguacu-three-days/) | Day 1 |
| [Incentive, 3 days](/brazil/tour/iguazu-incentive-3-days/) | Together with Macuco Safari |
| [Grand tour, 17 days](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) | Day 14 |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_brazil_foz_iguazu_three_days,tour_iguazu_incentive_3_days,tour_chile_argentina_private_grand_tour_17_days}}

## Combining the Bird Park and the waterfalls

The Bird Park is near the entrance to the Brazilian side of [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), so both can conveniently be visited in one day. The nature of the walks differs, however. At the falls, travelers follow panoramic paths overlooking the cascades; at the Bird Park, they observe Atlantic Forest birds close up.

According to Parque das Aves, its designated walking trail is approximately **2 km** long and passes through several large aviaries visitors can enter. Do not plan this part of the day as a rushed box-ticking exercise: stopping to observe and photograph birds takes time. Transfers and visits to the falls add to the walk, and Macuco Safari requires an additional boat excursion when selected.

The Argentine side needs separate logistics and a border crossing. [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/) are in a different section of the waterfall complex. Allocating two days to the two sides allows travelers to explore without fitting every crossing into a single schedule.

## Who the different itineraries suit

**Nature and bird lovers.** Check how much free time remains at the park after mandatory excursions. In the three-day tour, Iguazu's natural attractions are the main theme; in a multi-country journey, they form just one part. To compare this with observing wildlife in its natural habitat, explore [nature and wildlife tours in Brazil](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/) and the [Pantanal](/brazil/place/pantanal/). These are very different ways to experience fauna.

**Families with children.** The large aviaries, colorful birds and tree shade make the park interesting for families. Consider total time spent on your feet and the number of activities in a day, particularly if the waterfalls and boat trip are also scheduled. Do not assume a journey is specifically a family tour merely because it includes the Bird Park.

**Corporate groups.** The incentive program brings together the walk, waterfalls, boat trip and evening events. Compare these activities with participants' interests and the actual conditions: transport, meals, accommodation and the order of excursion days differ by product.

**Travelers seeing several countries.** Choose [multi-country tours](/multi-country/) according to their full geography and number of transfers. One Bird Park day alone does not determine the comfort of a 17-day journey.

## What to check before choosing

Confirm three facts in the specific tour: **whether dedicated time is allocated to the Bird Park, whether both sides of the falls are included and whether Macuco Safari is a core or optional activity**. On the three-day route with 4* accommodation, admission tickets for the principal excursions are included, while the boat trip costs extra. The corporate incentive has the boat in its schedule, but pricing is worked out individually.

If Iguazu gets only one day on a long journey, you may not be able to spend several hours with the birds. If the park is a priority, select a trip that devotes a meaningful part of the excursion day to it, rather than one where it appears only as a possible stop.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you see the Bird Park and Brazilian waterfalls in one day?

Yes. The sites are close together. The [three-day Iguazu tour](/brazil/tour/foz-do-iguacu-three-days/) schedules them on the same day. Adding Macuco Safari makes the timetable considerably busier.

### Is the Bird Park in Argentina?

No. Parque das Aves is in Brazil, at Foz do Iguaçu. Visits to the Argentine waterfalls are organized separately across the border.

### Are the park visit and boat trip included in every tour price?

Conditions vary. On the [standard three-day tour](/brazil/tour/foz-do-iguacu-three-days/), Macuco Safari is an optional extra. On the [three-day incentive itinerary](/brazil/tour/iguazu-incentive-3-days/), the boat trip is in the schedule. Refer to the published conditions of the chosen tour.

### How much time should I allow for the park itself?

The walking route covers about 2 km, but the actual time depends on stops, photography and group composition. Allow extra time to observe the birds, especially if you also plan to see the waterfalls that day.

## Petrópolis: an imperial city in the mountains near Rio

**Petrópolis offers a glimpse of 19th-century Brazil beyond the ocean coast.** The city lies in the mountains of Rio de Janeiro state and developed as a summer retreat for the imperial court. Its buildings, museums and streets reveal the period of the Second Empire and an aspect of Brazilian history rarely central to a beach holiday.

Unlike [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), where Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and beaches often dominate sightseeing, Petrópolis offers a calmer experience rich in history. Choose several important sites for a meaningful visit rather than trying to see the entire city on a brief excursion.

## The Imperial Museum: what is inside Pedro II's palace?

The **Museu Imperial** occupies a former residence of the Brazilian imperial family. The palace was constructed in the 19th century during Pedro II's reign. Today, its historic interiors, documents and collections are devoted to Brazil's monarchical era.

According to the museum, its permanent exhibition introduces the history of the state and the imperial court's daily life. Look at how objects relate to political history, social structures and the cultural tastes of the 19th century. Remember the social context as well: this period included slavery and the complicated process of abolition.

If you have a particular interest in history, leave time to read the museum's explanations rather than simply walk through the rooms. Gallery access, tickets and photography rules may change; check the official museum website for the relevant date.

## The Crystal Palace and historic center

The **Crystal Palace** is one of Petrópolis' recognizable attractions, a small pavilion made of metal and glass. It is connected with the city's history and used as a venue for cultural events. Whether the interior can be visited depends on current opening arrangements and events.

A city walk offers architecture from different eras, green streets and mountain scenery. It is an excellent way to change perspective after Rio, moving from its busy coastline to a historic center with a different climate and natural environment.

| Interest | Main stop |
|---|---|
| Monarchical history | Imperial Museum |
| Architecture | Palace and city center |
| City events | Crystal Palace |
| Walking | Historic streets and parks |

A museum visit is not the same as a general sightseeing walk. When a tour includes the word “Petrópolis,” it does not always mean tickets to every museum and guided interpretation are included.

## Arranging a journey from Rio de Janeiro

Petrópolis is in the mountains beyond Rio's urban area. The drive climbs into the hills, and traffic and weather affect the road. Arrange departure, museum times and the return in advance, especially if an international flight is scheduled for the following day.

We offer stand-alone excursions around Petrópolis as well as itineraries where the city can be added as an extra. Compare [tours visiting Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/tour/) and [culture and history journeys through Brazil](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/). The important distinction is between a full day featuring museum visits and an itinerary where Petrópolis is merely one possible side trip.

If your journey also covers the [Coffee Valley](/brazil/place/coffee-valley-rio-de-janeiro/), it reveals another part of Rio de Janeiro state's history. Nineteenth-century fazendas illustrate the rural economy, while Petrópolis' palace depicts the life and politics of the imperial family. They can be combined on an extended journey, but they are not nearby sights within walking distance of one another.

## How much time to leave and when to go

For the Imperial Museum, Crystal Palace and historic center, I recommend planning **a full day**. If you want other museums, architecture and walks, consider an overnight stay or an additional part of a day. This is guidance on duration, not a guarantee of included tour services.

The mountain climate differs from coastal Rio. Bring warmer clothes and rain protection, especially if you will spend a lot of time outdoors. Check museum closure days and visiting rules before planning your museum itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about Petrópolis

### Why is Petrópolis called the Imperial City?

The city is associated with summer stays by the Brazilian emperor Pedro II. Its historic legacy is represented above all by the Imperial Museum in the former palace.

### Is a day trip from Rio possible?

Yes, with an early departure and a well-planned route. Allow separate time for the mountain road and museum visits.

### Is Petrópolis part of the city of Rio?

No. It is a separate city in the mountainous part of Rio de Janeiro state, with its own history and attractions.

## Tours with an optional trip to Petrópolis from Rio de Janeiro

[Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/) lies in the mountains not far from [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Brazil's emperor Pedro II spent his summers here, and the former palace now houses the Imperial Museum. For travelers, it is an opportunity to discover historic architecture and 19th-century Brazil away from Rio's beach neighborhoods.

This directory brings together {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} where a trip to Petrópolis **can be added to the main itinerary**. The city is not a mandatory stop just because it appears in the full list of possible destinations. When choosing a tour, consider travel time, museum visits and the return journey separately.

## What to see in Petrópolis

The main attraction is the **Imperial Museum**, housed in Pedro II's former summer palace. Its collections cover Brazil's monarchical period, court culture and the city's development. The museum itself confirms that the building served as the emperor's summer residence. The exhibition helps explain Petrópolis' reputation as the Imperial City.

The historic center features the **Crystal Palace**, a metal-and-glass pavilion that has become one of the city's landmarks. Together with palace architecture, green avenues and mountain views, it creates a completely different impression of the Rio region.

The separate [Petrópolis description](/brazil/place/petropolis/) covers the Imperial Museum and Crystal Palace in more detail. For a full day, also consider the historic streets and walking areas. However, particular admission tickets, museum schedules and the route between sights must be confirmed within the selected excursion.

## When is it convenient to add the city?

On the [8-day “Rio and Iguazu with Brazil's Jewish Heritage” journey](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-jewish-heritage-8-days/), the main program focuses on Rio, the waterfalls and historical-cultural themes. Petrópolis is listed among additional geographical possibilities rather than mandatory stops. It should therefore be considered a separate outing during free time.

[Family journeys in Brazil](/brazil/tour/brazil-family-tour/) may include other trips beyond Rio. Consider the group's interests: children often benefit from alternating museums with walks, while adults who love history may want more time for exhibitions and architecture. Whether this extra trip works depends on the number of genuinely free days in Rio.

If a journey is full of flights between Iguazu, Amazonia and beach resorts, a trip into the mountains requires a separate block of time. A brief stop between two flights is not a proper visit to Petrópolis.

## How much time should you allocate?

A trip from Rio involves a drive into the mountains. Travel time depends on your departure neighborhood, road conditions and selected stops. For the Imperial Museum and Crystal Palace, plan a full sightseeing day rather than trying to fit them between other distant attractions.

Petrópolis is higher than coastal Rio, so the mountains can be cooler and the weather more changeable. Comfortable shoes are helpful for exploring the palace grounds and historic streets.

Museums may have closure days, special exhibitions and photography restrictions. Check schedules with the official institutions when planning. Mentioning a historic attraction in an excursion title does not guarantee access to its interiors on every date.

## How Petrópolis differs from an old Rio sightseeing tour

An ordinary [Rio sightseeing tour](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/sugarloaf-rio-city-four-hours/) covers cathedrals, colonial neighborhoods and city panoramas. Petrópolis reveals a different era, specifically the history of the imperial residence. If you want a deeper introduction to Brazil's monarchy, a trip into the mountains offers more than another brief stop in central Rio.

Compare the stand-alone [private Royal Petrópolis excursion](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/royal-petropolis-private-tour-full-day/) with the complete [directory of tours visiting Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/tour/). This helps you determine which historic sites are part of an actual program and which require an extra day.

## Frequently asked questions about optional Petrópolis visits

### Is Petrópolis mandatory on every tour listed?

No. This is a directory of programs where an **additional** city visit is possible. Whether the excursion, admission and transfers are included depends on the particular tour's conditions.

### Can you visit Petrópolis from Rio in one day?

Yes. Stand-alone excursion programs offer this format. Allow for the drive in both directions and museum opening hours.

### Which sights are especially interesting?

The Imperial Museum in Pedro II's former palace and the Crystal Palace. It is also worth leaving time to walk through the historic center.

### Is the trip suitable for families?

Yes, if participants are interested in history and comfortable with a full sightseeing day including travel. Arrange the actual route and duration in advance.
